inputs.text: In Paris, the conviction of Father Bernard Domini, superior of the Missionary Family of Notre-Dame, under France's new law against psychological subjection shows how religious institutions continue to exert coercive control over people. While this has stirred pushback from religious communities and civil liberties advocates who seem more focused on preserving traditional power structures, it represents a necessary step to shield vulnerable groups from the manipulative hierarchies that have long exploited inequality and dependency. These systems don't operate in isolation—they reflect deeper patterns of institutional dominance that progressive reforms must dismantle to protect individual autonomy.
